assumptions: All bought-part sizes are nominal and unmeasured. This covers the ESP32-C3 SuperMini (22.5 x 18, pin rows assumed 2x8 on 2.54 pitch, row spacing unmeasured), the 1.54in OLED (44 x 37 module, 36 x 19 view, 40 x 32 holes), SG90/FS90R servos, 18650 cells (65 mm unprotected assumed; protected cells up to 69 mm would hit the carrier at x=38), the charger, the buck module and the switch. Every team reconciles with measured parts at integration.

Uncertain hardware: the user has not named the 2S charger/protection module. It is assumed to be one all-in-one USB-C 2S board with protection and balance (B+/BM/B-/P+/P-), able to supply >=3 A. A 2S buck needs a low dropout because 2S can fall to about 6.0 V; MP1584-class modules work, Mini560-type fixed modules may not. Many 1.54in 128x64 OLEDs (SSD1309) ship in 7-pin SPI mode. An I2C 4-pin variant, or a jumper change, is assumed and the user must confirm.

The servo signal is 3.3 V logic into 5 V servos. This normally works for SG90/FS90R and is not verified. The expansion I2C/GPIO also uses 3.3 V logic. Expansion modules must accept 3.3 V signalling and draw no more than the 5 V budget left after the servos.

+5V is sealed at 5.0 V, not 6 V, because it also feeds the SuperMini 5V pin (on-board LDO input max about 6 V). The OR-ing diode to +5V_MCU, the 1000 uF bulk capacitor (>=10 V), the I2C pull-ups (target 4.7 k to +3V3), the battery divider (target 100k/33k + 100 nF), and any fuse or reverse-protection parts are internal to the board team. Their values are targets, not sealed limits. Only the net names and connector pins are sealed.

The carrier board is a dummy/ERC board representing the hand-wired build. Off-board modules (buck, charger, switch, fan, OLED, servos) appear on it only as connectors. The board team may add a harness table but must not change connector pin orders.

Mechanical frame from the draft: the crank axes sit 10 mm above the body bottom (draft zO = 42.47 above ground, so ground is about z -32.5). Crank axles are at x = +/-27.3 and drive gears at x = +/-13.1, z 21.1. The lid is 2.5 mm thick on a 28.5 mm frame. The expansion deck has 8 posts on a 15 mm grid around (-5,0) on top of the lid (z 31..37) plus a 12 mm cable hole at (-5,0). The fan and OLED lid features are as listed in modules. Lid screws (4x M3 self-tap) are case-owned.

Changes from the draft, with reasons: (1) The back-wall USB opening stays 24 (Y) x 18 (Z) at y 12.5 but moves to z centre 12 (draft 14), so the charger USB-C is centred while the module stays below the fan (z <= 18.5). (2) The switch hole moves to y -10, z 11 (draft y -14, z 14) so it clears the fan and the buck bay. (3) A new front-wall USB-C service slot, 14 (Y) x 9 (Z) centred at (y 0, z 11.9), lets the user flash the SuperMini later without opening the case. (4) The carrier replaces the draft's bare board posts at (49+/-6.5, +/-9) with 4 M2 posts at the board mounts, 3 mm tall on the floor (board bottom z 5.0).

Servo envelopes are draft-derived references: the body hangs inside the wall, flange outside, and extends away from the body centre. The case team owns the servo seat and gear/leg geometry. It may move the servos by up to 5 mm in X/Z to fix weak spots, provided they stay clear of every electronic module envelope above and the cables still reach J3-J6. Board and firmware do not depend on servo position.

Known draft risks the case must resolve. The wall above the servo window is only about 1.3 mm (needs >= 2 mm, for example by lowering the drive-gear angle g_driver_dir or adding an outside rib; the body height stays sealed at 31). The horizontal axle studs need support, so use chamfer/gusset roots, self-supporting 45-degree undersides or split-print pins. The draft subtracts the servo cutouts after adding the lid posts at (+/-25, +/-32.3), which probably cuts the posts, so check servo-to-post clearance and move the posts if needed.

The overall mechanical envelope [160,150,70] (X,Y,Z) is the sealed limit, including leg sweep, ground to the top of the deck posts. The draft's Jansen joints reach about x +/-72.3 (about 153 mm with link bosses), so the brief's 126 mm length is the body only. Width is about 143 and height about 69.5 from the draft.

Numeric targets chosen by the lead and owned by the teams: battery 0%/100% at 6.4/8.4 V, low-battery cutoff 6.6 V, 1 s command watchdog, nudge pulse length, carrier height limit tolerance. Teams may tune these and report them at integration.

Wire harness routing between the rear power bay (CHG1, SW1, BUCK1) and the front carrier runs under the lid above the cells or along the side gaps. The case team provides a channel or clips. Harness lengths are reconciled at integration.
Nothing is flashed, printed, powered, run or ordered by any team.

coordinateFrame.axes: +X = forward (front legs, OLED, ESP32 side). +Y = robot left. +Z = up (right-handed). Leg names: FL = (+X,+Y), FR = (+X,-Y), RL = (-X,+Y), RR = (-X,-Y). Module positionMm = centre of the envelope box [x,y,z]. sizeMm = full box size [dx,dy,dz]. KiCad uses Y pointing down, so the board team maps contract (x,y) to KiCad (x, -y) plus a fixed offset and reports that offset.
coordinateFrame.origin: Body footprint centre (X/Y centre of the 126 x 75 body box) on the underside of the frame floor. The body box spans x -63..63, y -37.5..37.5, z 0..31 (frame z 0..28.5, lid z 28.5..31, corner radius 6). The ground plane where the feet stand is about z = -32.5 (from the draft; reference only). Crank/drive axes lie along Y.

firmwareBehavior: Target: ESP32-C3 SuperMini (Arduino-ESP32 core via PlatformIO, USB-CDC on boot). Compile only. Never flashed by any team.

The pin map comes only from the contract pins: servos FL=GPIO5, FR=GPIO6, RL=GPIO7, RR=GPIO10. I2C SDA=GPIO8, SCL=GPIO9 at 400 kHz. VBAT_SENSE=GPIO3 (ADC1, 11 dB attenuation, averaged). EXP_IO_A=GPIO4 and EXP_IO_B=GPIO1 boot as high-Z inputs. GPIO0/2/20/21 are left untouched. The on-board LED shares GPIO8 (SDA), so firmware never drives it.

Boot: servo PWM outputs stay off (no pulses) until the gait engine starts. Then every servo gets 50 Hz pulses in a 1000-2000 us window. The per-servo neutral (stop) pulse defaults to 1500 us and can be trimmed per servo. Each servo has a direction sign because the left and right sides are mirrored. Trims, signs and leg phase offsets are saved in NVS.

Wi-Fi: starts a SoftAP named 'NautilusDog-XXXX' (last MAC bytes) with WPA2 and a per-device password (shown on the OLED). The control page is at http://192.168.4.1. The OLED first shows a Wi-Fi-join QR code, then the URL QR. After a client connects it shows a smiley face plus battery %.
OLED: 128x64 SSD1309/SSD1306 over I2C (U8g2). Address 0x3C by default, 0x3D configurable. Display rotation and controller type are compile-time constants, to be checked against the real module.

Web page (served from flash, WebSocket control): forward / back / left / right / stop buttons, speed slider 0-100%, gait selector (trot = diagonal pairs FL+RR and FR+RL held 180 degrees apart), live battery %.

Calibration page: for each leg, nudge buttons rotate that servo by a short timed pulse in either direction. Also: set stop trim, mark the current leg pose as phase zero, and save to NVS. Servos are open-loop with no angle feedback, so phase comes from timing using a per-servo seconds-per-revolution value that is calibrated and stored.
Turning is done by giving the left and right sides different speeds. Reverse runs the cranks backward.
Safety: if no WebSocket command or heartbeat arrives for 1 s, all servos stop at neutral. Below the low-battery cutoff, servos stop and the OLED shows a warning.

Battery %: VBAT = ADC volts x divider ratio. The default ratio constant is (100k+33k)/33k, matching the board team's target divider, and is reconciled at integration. 2S 6.4 V = 0%, 8.4 V = 100%, piecewise-linear. Default low-battery cutoff target: 6.6 V.
The fan is always on in hardware. Firmware does not control it.

modules.interface: The native KiCad carrier board (dummy, ERC/DRC only, never ordered). Its outline and mounts are given in board. J1-J9 are 2.54 mm headers. Sits on 4 case posts (M2 self-tap), board bottom at z=5.0
Keep-out above the carrier board top (z 6.6..20.6): every carrier component and header with mating plug must stay inside it. The case keeps it clear. The OLED's underside clearance starts at z 22.4

U1 on the carrier through 2x8 2.54 pins, PCB bottom 2.5 mm above the carrier top (z 9.1). Long axis along X. USB-C faces +X with its centre at (60.75, 0, 11.9), lined up with the front-wall service slot
DISP1. Hangs under the lid, view window in the lid centred at (39,0) 36 (X) x 19 (Y). Module mount holes at 40 x 32 (X x Y) around (39,0). Hand-wired to J7
FAN1 under the lid, exhausts up and out through a 27 mm lid opening at (-45.5,0). 4 x 3.2 mm holes on a 23 mm square. Wired to J8, always on
2 x 18650 lying along X at y = +/-10.5, centres at z 12.75, in printed cradle ribs. Cell envelope plus tabs and wiring. Wired to CHG1 B+/BM/B-
CHG1 all-in-one 2S USB-C charger + protection module. Its USB-C faces -X through the back-wall opening, receptacle centre at (-61, 12.5, 12). Sits on case standoffs
BUCK1 module (for example MP1584-class, 22 x 17), set to 5.0 V. Flat in the rear-right bay, held with a case clip or tape. VBAT_SW in, +5V out to J1
SW1 panel switch in a 7 mm round hole in the back wall centred at (y -10, z 11). Body inside the wall (x -61..-49). Switches VBAT_PACK to VBAT_SW

360-degree micro servo (SG90/FS90R), drive axis along +Y through the left wall at (x 13.1, z 21.1). The envelope is the body part inside the frame; flange, shaft and horn are outside the wall. Cable to J3
Same as servo_FL, mirrored to the right wall: drive axis at (x 13.1, z 21.1), cable to J4
Same as servo_FL, mirrored to the rear-left: drive axis at (x -13.1, z 21.1), cable to J5
Same as servo_FL, mirrored to the rear-right: drive axis at (x -13.1, z 21.1), cable to J6

A 6-wire harness from J9 ends in a 1x6 female 2.54 housing with the same pin order as J9. It is stowed under the lid next to the 12 mm deck cable hole at (-5,0) so it can be pulled out through the hole

interfaces.name: Robot Chó Nautilus V0 – shared interface contract r001

pins.signal: Battery sense ADC (ADC1_CH3, divided VBAT_SW, <=2.1 V)

powerRails.name: VBAT_PACK
powerRails.source: 2x 18650 in series (2S, 6.0-8.4 V) through the all-in-one 2S USB-C charger/protection module P+ output; P- is system GND

powerRails.name: VBAT_SW
powerRails.source: VBAT_PACK after power switch SW1 on the back wall (6.0-8.4 V). Feeds the buck VIN and carrier J2 (battery sense)

powerRails.name: +5V
powerRails.source: Off-board buck module, >=3 A, set to 5.0 V. Feeds the 4 servos, the fan, the expansion header and +5V_MCU. Enters the carrier at J1. The 1000 uF bulk capacitor sits on the carrier

powerRails.name: +5V_MCU
powerRails.source: +5V through a carrier-side Schottky/OR-ing diode into the ESP32-C3 SuperMini 5V pin. Stops the SuperMini USB-C from back-feeding the servos while flashing

powerRails.name: +3V3
powerRails.source: The ESP32-C3 SuperMini's on-board LDO (3V3 pin). Feeds the OLED and the I2C pull-ups only

powerRails.name: USB_VBUS_CHG
powerRails.source: USB-C charging input on the charger/protection module behind the back-wall opening. Not on the carrier

powerRails.name: GND
powerRails.source: Common return. This is the charger/protection module P- net

tasks.board: Build the native KiCad carrier board 'nautilus-dog-carrier' (dummy/ERC board, never ordered) exactly to this contract. Outline is a 22 x 52 rectangle x 38..60, y -26..26, 1.6 mm thick, with 4 x 2.2 mm M2 holes MH1-MH4. Footprints: U1 ESP32-C3 SuperMini as a 2x8 2.54 header footprint with USB-C at the +X edge, plus J1-J9 2.54 headers with the sealed pin orders and nets. Internal circuits are yours: the +5V to +5V_MCU OR-ing Schottky, 1000 uF >=10 V bulk capacitor on +5V near J1 and the servo headers (lay it flat if needed to stay under the 14 mm height limit above the board top), 100 nF decoupling, 4.7 k I2C pull-ups to +3V3, and the VBAT_SW divider (target 100k/33k + 100 nF) into VBAT_SENSE. Put no-connect flags on GPIO0/2/20/21 and use correct power flags. Keep every part inside carrier_component_zone. Run native KiCad ERC and DRC to clean with no weakened rules, waivers or relaxed manufacturing checks. Publish the off-board harness table (BUCK1, SW1, CHG1, FAN1, DISP1, servos, expansion pigtail) and the contract-to-KiCad coordinate offset. Do not order or touch hardware.
tasks.case: In case/, build the full printable case and mechanism from the cadsmith draft (prompts/assets/cadsmith-draft-model.py) in this contract's frame (origin at the body-bottom centre, so translate the draft by z -32.47). Parts: frame and lid (126 x 75 x 31 body, corner radius 6, 4x M3 self-tap lid screws), 4 leg modules (nautilus drive and crank gear pair, Jansen links, M2 screw + nut joints), carrier posts at MH1-MH4 (M2 self-tap, board bottom z 5.0), standoffs/clips for CHG1 and BUCK1, battery cradle, sealed wall openings (back-wall USB 24 x 18 at y 12.5 z 12, switch 7 mm at y -10 z 11, front USB-C service slot 14 x 9 at y 0 z 11.9), lid OLED window and holes, fan opening and holes, expansion deck posts with heat-set pockets and the 12 mm cable hole, the expansion pigtail stow/clip, and harness channels. Keep every module envelope clear and the whole robot inside 160 x 150 x 70 including leg sweep. Fix the known weak spots (>=2 mm wall above the servo windows, support-free or minimal-support axle studs, servo vs lid-post clearance) and record every change from the draft with its reason. Produce separate TEST ONLY / MATING_TEST prints first: a servo seat coupon, one nautilus gear pair on its axles, and one leg joint. Then the full set with print orientation. Do not print or slice to a printer.
tasks.firmware: In firmware/, write the PlatformIO Arduino-ESP32 project for the ESP32-C3 SuperMini directly from the contract pin map, with no board handoff needed. It must include: a pins/config header (servo GPIO5/6/7/10, I2C 8/9, VBAT_SENSE GPIO3, EXP 4/1, divider ratio constant, OLED address/controller/rotation constants), a LEDC 50 Hz continuous-servo driver with per-servo neutral trim and direction sign, an open-loop phase/timing gait engine (trot, forward/back/turn, speed), SoftAP + QR (Wi-Fi join and URL) on the OLED via U8g2 followed by a smiley face + battery %, a WebSocket web UI (drive buttons, speed, gait, battery %), a calibration page (per-leg nudge, trim, phase zero, NVS save), a 1 s command watchdog stop and a low-battery stop. Compile only if a toolchain is present. Never flash or connect to hardware. The README documents the pin map, defaults, and the calibration steps for the user.
